essential: The opening: other careers fail; Darwin and Lyell (intimate at the Legation, but neither Darwin nor anyone meets Adams). The new theories must be taken on trust, and Adams is helpless in mathematics.
He fails to become a Marxist and becomes a Comteist within evolution, eager to see the world upset.

Geology as the easier route. Lyell's 'Principles' leads from Selection to Uniformity, a seductive unity after the war's enforcement of unity. Adams offers to review Lyell for America; the Pendennis joke.
The Newton/apple analogy: ignorance must begin at the beginning.
The glacial epoch looks like a chasm; the provocative inserted sentence on Agassiz draws no reply from Lyell.
Terebratula as too much uniformity. The first vertebrate lies under Adams's favorite Abbey on Wenlock Edge. Give minimal local context: the Wenlock Abbey of his English friends the Milnes Gaskells.
The Wenlock Edge meditation: time-sequences interchangeable, Pteraspis as ancestor, the Cambrian void beyond. The La Fontaine wolf verse and his doubt about moral evolution after the war.
Pteraspis older than evolution; Limulus remembered from Quincy Bay; the vertebrate appearing complete; Lyell's theory as pure inference like Paley's watch; only coal-power asserts evolution.

Confession: no Faith, Motion and Change, 'Darwinian for fun'. He nonetheless locks up psychology and resolves to follow Law, Evolution and Unity as Will, at any cost. Note that the path later 'sacrificed much more'.

Specie payments: his research shows restriction was a mistake, a dangerous finding for State Street. The two finance articles are accepted, giving him rank on the North American Review. Describe the Review's character (small circulation, five dollars a page).
No contemporary could be picked for success in 1867.

Last year in England: happiest, 'Silurian horizon'; Rome and the steps of Ara Coeli again with Milnes Gaskell (a friend); departure from Liverpool having learned nothing but English habit, 'an old and rather worn suit of clothes'.

title: DARWINISM (1867-1868)

verbatim.text: Henry Adams was Darwinist because it was easier than not, for his ignorance exceeded belief
it was the very best substitute for religion; a safe, conservative, practical, thoroughly Common-Law deity.

verbatim.purpose: An image of passivity before force that anticipates the dynamic theory.
verbatim.text: One had been, from the first, dragged hither and thither like a French poodle on a string, following always the strongest pull
the first vertebrate was a very respectable fish
he could prove only Evolution that did not evolve; Uniformity that was not uniform; and Selection that did not select.
what he valued most was Motion, and that what attracted his mind was Change.
He was a Darwinian for fun.

voice_profile: Third-person autobiography in which the old Adams ironically judges young 'Henry Adams' or 'the private secretary'. It moves from concrete scene to aphorism ('a friend in power is a friend lost'), deflates itself constantly ('insect', 'worm', 'small fry'), and builds long periodic sentences out of semicolon series and dashes. It returns to the vocabulary of 'education', 'force', 'unity' and 'chaos'. Irony works through reversal: the lesson learned proves wrong, and the evidence arrives forty years too late. The past perspective of 1862 and the retrospect of the 1900s run side by side and must stay clearly distinguished. Quoted documents, such as letters, despatches and diary entries, serve as evidence that ironizes the narrator's certainties.
